response: Yes, specialty care is associated with improved survival of patients with congestive heart failure. Studies have shown that patients with congestive heart failure who receive care from cardiologists or other specialists tend to have better outcomes, including higher survival rates, compared to those who receive care from general practitioners or non-specialists. This is likely due to specialists' greater expertise and experience in managing complex heart failure cases, as well as their ability to provide more targeted and evidence-based treatments.
